THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE UMESH M ADIGA
ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the insurer challenging the judgment and award dated 12.11.2021 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and (for short `Tribunal'), in MVC No.452/2016, questioning the quantum of compensation.
2. Though this appeal is slated for admission, with consent of learned advocates appearing for both the sides, it is taken up for final disposal.
NC: 2025:KHC:51100 HC-KAR 3.
For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.
4. The brief facts of the case are that, on 27.11.2015 at about 8.00 p.m, the claimant/petitioner was coming from Hassan circle to I.B. Circle as a pedestrian on the left side of N.H.206 road.
At Government Boys College, he met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-44-R-1719, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he has suffered from permanent disability.

With these M/S The Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs Sri. Satishkumar G.K on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48150307/
2 reasons, the claimant has prayed for awarding the compensation.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs Sri. Satishkumar G.K
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. The respondent No.1 was the owner and respondent No.2 was the insurer of the offending motorcycle.
Respondent No.2-insurer in its written statement denied the petition averments and denied its liability and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
6. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal framed necessary issues.
NC: 2025:KHC:51100 HC-KAR 7.
The claimant to prove his case, examined two witnesses as PW-1 and PW-2 and marked 10 documents, as per Exs.P-1 to P-10.
The respondent-Insurance Company did not examine any witness but marked Exs.R-1 - true copy of the policy.

8. The Tribunal after hearing both parties and appreciating the evidence on record, by the impugned judgment, awarded the following amount of compensation:
 Particulars Amount in Rs.
Injury, pain and sufferings 1,00,000
Medical expenses 31,200  Future medical expenses 15,000  Loss of earning during bed rest 27,000  Loss of future earning capacity 1,36,080  prospects
Food, transport, conveyance, 10,000  amenities, nourishment  Total 3,19,280  9.
Heard the arguments of the learned counsel appearing for the claimant as well as the insurer.
10. The fact of the accident and injuries sustained by the claimant are not in serious dispute.
Therefore, there is no need to reconsider the same.
The learned counsel for the appellant contends that claimant has contributed for causing accident in question.

Unmindfully, he was trying to cross the road for taking photos, at that time,
incident occurred.
The Tribunal has not considered the same.
The learned counsel for respondent/claimant contends that at the time of accident, the claimant was not crossing the road as per his pleadings and evidence.
Therefore, the contention of the appellant that he had contributed for the accident in question is not tenable.

M/S The Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs Sri. Satishkumar G.K on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48150307/
3 12.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs Sri. Satishkumar G.K
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The submission of learned counsel for the respondent is tenable.
It is the pleading and evidence of PW-1 that while he was going from Hassan circle towards I.B. circle on foot path, the rider of the motor cycle came from his back side and hit him.
He has not at all pleaded or stated that while crossing the road the accident occurred.
Therefore, contention of the insurer that when claimant was taking photos accident occurred is not at all case made out by the claimant.
Therefore, there are no reason to hold that claimant had contributed in occurrence of the accident.
The learned counsel for the appellant contends that reasons stated by the Trial Court while assessment of compensation are not consistent.
The Tribunal in paragraph No.17 of the impugned judgment assessed disability as 12% to the whole body.
In paragraph No.24 also, disability is assessed as 12%.
But while calculating the amount of compensation, disability is taken as 19%.
According to the case of claimant, he was aged about 33 years.
The Tribunal without any basis assessed the multiplier as '18' instead of '16'.
Even the amount awarded by the Tribunal under the head loss of future earning capacity due to permanent disability is also not correct.
Therefore, prays to set aside the same.
14. The submission of learned counsel for the appellant in this regard is tenable.
Tribunal in paragraph No.24 considered the permanent disability and determined it as 12% to the whole body.
But in later part of same paragraph, while calculating the compensation it has taken 19% and applied multiplier as '18' instead of '16'.
This needs correction.
The appellant could have filed a review petition before the very same court instead of filing this appeal.

The Tribunal calculated NC:
2025:KHC:51100 HC-KAR the compensation under the head 'loss of future earning capacity due to permanent disability' as under (Rs.9,000x12x18x7%=Rs.1,36,080/-).
The Tribunal has neither taken disability as 12% or 19%, but suddenly took disability as 7%.
In fact, claimant is entitled for the compensation under the head 'loss of future earning capacity due to permanent disability' as (Rs.9,000x12x16x12%=Rs.2,07,260/-).

The learned counsel for the appellant submits that the said correction need not be incorporated in the order,
which would prejudice the case of insurance company.
The said contention is not acceptable.
It is a beneficial legislation.
If there is an arithmetical mistakes it shall be corrected, when it is noticed by the Court.
15. On re-appreciation of the materials, the amount awarded by the Tribunal under the head 'pain and suffering' is on the higher side.
Looking at the materials, claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head 'Pain and suffering.'
16. The learned counsel for the appellant seriously challenges the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal.
NC: 2025:KHC:51100 HC-KAR Awarding of interest is at the discretion of the Tribunal as per Section 171 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988.

The Tribunal assigned the reason and followed the M/S The Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs Sri. Satishkumar G.K on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48150307/
4 judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Jithendra Khimshankar Trivedi and others vs. Kasam Daud Kumbhar and others1 and awarded the rate of interest.

entities.text: Jithendra Khimshankar Trivedi and others vs. Kasam Daud Kumbhar and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said finding does not call for any interference.
17. The learned counsel for the appellant relies on the judgment in the case of Joyeeta Bose and Others vs. Venkateshan.

entities.text: Joyeeta Bose and Others vs. Venkateshan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: V and Others decided on 27.08.2020 in MFA No.5896/2018 and connected matters and submits that the Division Bench of this Court held that interest shall be awarded at the rate of 6% per annum.
He further stated that according to Section 34 of CPC, interest shall be awarded at the rate of 6% per annum.
Thus, contended that interest awarded is on the higher side.
18. The Tribunal has relied on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court stated above while awarding the rate of interest.

Moreover, if the interest awarded by the Tribunal is (2015) 3 CLJ 668 sc NC:
2025:KHC:51100 HC-KAR unjust then only this Court has to interfere in the said finding.
Since it is based on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court, there is no need to reconsider the same.
19. The claimant is entitled for following amount of compensation:

Particulars Amount in Rs.
 Pain and sufferings 50,000  Medical expenses 31,200  Future medical expenses 15,000  Loss of earning during laid up period 27,000  (Rs.9,000x3)
 Loss of future earning capacity due to 2,07,360  permanent disability  (Rs.9,000x12x16x12%)
Food, transport, conveyance, 10,000  amenities, nourishment  Total 3,40,560 20.
In all, claimant is entitled for Rs.3,40,560/- as against Rs.3,19,280/- awarded by the Tribunal.
21. Claimant is entitled for interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the petition till its realisation.
Undisputedly, respondent is liable to pay the same.

22. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:

ii) The judgment and award dated  12.11.2021 passed by the Senior Civil  Judge and JMFC, Tiptur in MVC  No.452/2016, stands modified.

sentences.text: iii) The claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.3,40,560/- as against Rs.3,19,280/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
iv) The respondent No-2 - Insurance  Company shall deposit the amount within a period of six weeks from the date of award.
v) The remaining portion of the award of the Tribunal shall remain unaltered.

vi) Draw award accordingly.
